talking_points.headline: ADGM adds a digital-asset wealth competitor
talking_points.context_html: Arab Bank Switzerland ME Ltd says it has received ADGM authorization and begun advising institutional and high-net-worth clients on digital assets. This adds a regional competitor offering, making regulatory permissions and the boundaries of advice and asset services relevant comparison criteria for wealth delivery. The supplied announcement does not report client uptake or operational performance.

AI & Technology.title: Major Banks Move to Block or Limit Customer-Directed AI Agents - The National Law Review
AI & Technology.summary: The article says JPMorgan Chase, Charles Schwab, Citigroup and Wells Fargo moved in October 2026 to block or contractually reallocate risk for third-party AI agents using customers’ credentials to access accounts; it contrasts these restrictions with permitted read-only open-banking connections. It describes security, fraud, deposit and liability concerns, alongside unsettled open-banking rules. For bank change teams, the distinction between credential-based access and controlled, authorized data connections is relevant to access design and accountability; the article’s legal and market characterizations are not evidence of a settled regulatory position.

Competitor Intelligence.title: Error
Competitor Intelligence.summary: Wealthsimple announced Penny, an AI assistant that can prepare transfers, payments and trades within its platform, with customer approval required before execution. The company says Penny uses a secure data feed rather than screen scraping or customer banking credentials; it plans to enable access through ChatGPT and Claude in early 2027, also subject to customer approval. This illustrates a fintech approach that combines assistance with transaction approval, but the article leaves responsibility for losses from AI errors unresolved and does not establish customer adoption or performance.

Competitor Intelligence.title: DBS Profit Misses Estimates on Trading Drop, Names Lim Chair - Bloomberg.com
Competitor Intelligence.summary: Bloomberg reports that DBS’s third-quarter net profit fell 5% year over year to S$2.81 billion for the three months ended 30 September, below the surveyed analyst average, with weaker trading income offsetting gains in lending and wealth. The report also notes DBS announced a new chairman. The results provide a current competitor performance signal, but the excerpt does not give wealth-specific results or explain the causes of the trading-income decline beyond the stated market impact.

Competitor Intelligence.title: DBS Names Anthony Lim as Chairman From January 2027
Competitor Intelligence.summary: DBS named Anthony Lim as chairman from 1 January 2027, succeeding Peter Seah, who will leave the boards on 31 December 2026 and serve as senior adviser for one year. Lim has served on DBS’s boards since April 2020 and chaired its Compensation and Management Development Committee. The succession is a governance change at a major regional competitor; the report does not describe a new strategy or operating programme.

Private Banking & Wealth.title: Arab Bank Switzerland opens Abu Dhabi office and names Valérie Noël Chief Executive Officer - ADGM
Private Banking & Wealth.summary: Arab Bank Switzerland ME Ltd began operations in ADGM after receiving Financial Services Permission from the FSRA and appointed Valérie Noël as CEO. The entity says it will advise institutional, fintech, family-office and high-net-worth clients on digital assets within ADGM’s regulatory framework. This adds a competitor offering in Abu Dhabi’s digital-asset wealth market; the supplied material does not detail its operating model, client uptake or service outcomes.
